newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CSSD SAYS HOUSE MUST VET BANK SELLOFFS - CTK.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CSSD SAYS HOUSE MUST VET BANK SELLOFFS - CTK.

text.p: The strongest Czech opposition party, the Social Democrats (CSSD), wants the privatisation of major state-controlled commercial banks to be decided by the parliament, the local CTK agency reported on Monday.
"The concept of big commercial bank privatisation must be presented to the parliament and approved by it," CTK quoted a statement approved by CSSD's executive board as saying.
"The CSSD takes a irresponsible current attempts for a quick sell-off of these banks as a measure to stick holes in the state budget's incomes," it said.
Calls on Monday to party leadership to discuss the issue further were unsuccessful.

The CSSD holds 61 seats in the 200-seat lower house including the post of Chairman. Combined with votes from the extreme Republican and Communist members of the opposition, control enough votes to block the minority government's wishes.
But the three-party right wing coalition government says it has the executive power, under existing laws on privatisation, to conclude strategic selloffs.

The government has said it would like to privatise the remaining shares it holds in the Big Four Czech banks, which control roughly 70 percent of the country's banking activity, but CSSD has been cool to the plans.
The finance ministry is organising a tender to sell a roughly one-third stake in the fourth largest bank IPB a.s..
Privatisation of the country's four largest banks, in which the state throughout its National Property Fund holds the stakes, has been expected by investors for several years.
The NPF's chairman, Roman Ceska, said Japanese investment bank Nomura, had the best chance to win the tender, but he also said that he hoped the tender would be transparent.
The government retains large stakes, held by the NPF, in in IPB, Komercni Banka, Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. and Ceska Sporitelna.

CSSD'S leadership conditioned bank privatisations on "cultivation and civilisation of the market, owner's responsibility, a long-term perspective of the banking sector and its participation of the reconstruction of the economy", CTK reported.
